text.p: A California Appeals Court reinstated a lawsuit brought by salaried retirees of the Hughes Aircraft Co, according to the law firm representing the workers.

In a statement, the law firm of Sipser, Weinstock, Harper and Dorn said the lawsuit seeks to compel Hughes and its pension plan to turn over in excess of $1 billion in pension surplus to participants of the plan.
The suit was brought as a class action on behalf of all plan participants. Hughes Aircraft is a unit of General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp.

The suit, which was brought under the federal law protecting workers' pensions, alleges that over $1 billion in surplus assets has accumulated in the pension plan and that Hughes is using this surplus for its own benefit.

The retiree suit alleges that the surplus was due in part to the retirees' own contributions to the plan, but that none of it is being passed back to them. The suit seeks to have all or a portion of the surplus turned over to plan participants in the form of increased pension benefits.
GM is currently negotiating the sale of Hughes' defense operations to Raytheon Co
